module.purpose: Provides reusable Vitest assertions for booking scenarios, validating emails, webhooks, database records, calendar operations, video meetings, and workflow notifications.
module.summary: This test utility module centralizes behavioral assertions for booking-related integrations. It extends Vitest with an email matcher that parses HTML and iCalendar content, provides webhook payload assertions, checks persistence through a Prisma mock, and validates calendar and video-service call recordings. Helper functions encode expected booking lifecycle notifications, recurrence formatting, attendee visibility, integration failures, rescheduling, payment initiation, and absence of unwanted side effects.
module.businessContext: Supports automated testing of scheduling, booking, notification, calendar, video, payment, and webhook workflows. Failures indicate regressions in customer communications, booking persistence, integrations, or event lifecycle behavior.

assumptions.description: Callers provide populated email, SMS, calendar, video, and Prisma mock fixtures.
Webhook request bodies are JSON strings when inspected through fetchMock.
Captured emails expose to, subject, html, and icalEvent fields.
Booking URLs fall back to WEBSITE_URL when a booking origin is absent.

ambiguities.question: Should vi.waitFor calls be awaited by callers to guarantee notification assertions complete?
Is the unused organizer parameter in several expectation helpers intentional?
Should paid and unpaid webhook payload formats be unified?

concurrencyModel.notes: Most assertions are synchronous, database assertions are async, and round-robin notification checks invoke vi.waitFor without awaiting it.
